verdict.rationale: GitCafe documents pull requests as its own capability: opening them, reviewing diffs with feedback, stacked PRs, and rulesets that require PRs and reviews before merging. Nothing in the evidence mentions forking a repository or outside contributors without write access opening PRs from their own copies, so the fork-based half of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: documented fork capability, cross-repository (fork-to-upstream) pull requests, outside-contributor permission model, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an open-source-maintainer, I can let outside contributors fork my repository and propose changes back via pull requests

citations.quote: Browse files, compare diffs, and leave feedback alongside the code.
Build on an open pull request. Review each change separately, then merge the stack in order.
A ruleset protects matching branches or tags: it can require pull requests, reviews and passing checks
`cafe stack submit` pushes each commit after the base as its own branch and opens or reuses one pull request per commit.
